Hover a phrase for its gloss — transliteration, vocabulary, meaning, the way the reading editions set them. Click a sentence to replay the video from its beginning; the greyed lines around the spoken one are its context and stay hoverable too. Shift-click a phrase to copy it (the whole caption, if you shift-click beside one; the cloud has a copy button too). Alt-click (or Ctrl-click) a word to turn the text into a card — or use the “+ card” button inside any gloss cloud for the whole phrase. The card goes to an Anki deck, to one of your exercise decks, or onto the clipboard as markdown for a studio document. It can carry the word's own sound, cut with “🔊 cut the audio…”: from the film, for a film on this machine; from a recording of this tab, for a YouTube video in Chrome or Edge. The cloud is where a phrase is written too: the four dots mark it in the reading editions' own colours, and ✎ edit opens its fields — the text, the transliteration, the vocabulary, the meaning — and saves them into this video's annotations.

works in any browser on any of the toolbox's https addresses (the browser asked you once about the certificate — that was it). In Chrome pick “This Tab”; in Firefox share this browser window (or the screen) and keep the player visible — two coloured dots flash on the video's corners while the capture finds the exact video area. Sharing stays on, so later captures are instant, and in Chrome and Edge the same share lets “cut the audio…” record a YouTube video's sound (leave “Also allow tab audio” on). A paused video rolls in muted from ~5 seconds before the moment — YouTube keeps its overlay up that long — so the controls fade out of the shot, and it freezes back on the exact frame
